text:
maria (Support): heads up — we're getting 3 escalations this morning where streaming SSE sessions disconnect after ~30s and users get partial outputs + duplicate billing on retry. stack: hosted API, node client. sample case from customer A attached.

jin (Eng-runtime): ugh. are these TCP-level disconnects or application idle timeouts? any consistent error codes in client logs?

maria (Support): client logs show `ECONNRESET` after a burst of tokens, no HTTP 5xx. server logs show the connection still alive for another minute before we forcibly closed it. no `close` event from client reported.

alex (SRE): sounds like glibc/tcp keepalive or LB idle-probe mismatch. what does our loadbalancer idle timeout =?

jin (Eng-runtime): LB idle timeout is 60s for the cluster. but node client's default `keepAlive` on sockets might be 0 (disabled). if client doesn't emit any bytes, LB may drop. for SSE we usually send comment pings `:\n\n` every 15s. do we have that on the hosted path?

maria (Support): i thought we relied on the agent to stream heartbeat events, but not seeing consistent pings. some streams show `: ping` comments, others nothing.

alex (SRE): action: confirm if our proxy (ingress-nginx) is stripping or buffering `:\n` lines. there was a change last month around proxy buffering.

carla (Billing): also FYI billing team saw increases in token usage for these customers — looks like clients reconnecting and resuming requests, causing duplicate tokens billed. we don't dedupe partials today. customers complain.

jin (Eng-runtime): we should separate two problems: 1) detect dead connections reliably (so server can free resources and avoid half-open billing), 2) client recon/resume semantics to avoid double-charge.

maria (Support): quick repro steps i asked for and got from customer A:
```
# simplified repro
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/gen?model=xx \
  --no-buffer
# client then pauses for 40s, gets ECONNRESET
```
They also tried a node ws client with default socket keepalive off.

jin (Eng-runtime): proposed server-side changes:
- emit regular SSE comment pings every 12s (`:\n`) on all streams (hosted + dedicated)
- expose `x-last-event-id` / `Last-Event-ID` so clients can resume idempotently
- set an application-level inactivity timeout (e.g., 90s) after which we close the stream and mark it as aborted for billing purposes

alex (SRE): i support comment pings but we need to verify they survive the proxy chain. also ensure TCP keepalive configured on backend connections: `tcp_keepalive_time=120` etc. but that is coarse. user-level pings are more reliable.

carla (Billing): the billing policy implications: when a stream is closed by the server due to inactivity, billing should prorate tokens consumed until closure, but when client reconnect/resume we should avoid recharging tokens for overlapping output. we need an idempotency token or sequence cursor.

jin (Eng-runtime): agree. implementation idea: attach a `stream_id` and incremental `offset` on each event metadata. when a client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID: <stream_id>:<offset>` we can dedupe. minimal server store: keep recent stream cursors in redis for 10 minutes.

maria (Support): can we give interim workaround to customers? what to tell them right now to avoid regen charges?

alex (SRE): workaround: enable client TCP keepalive and have the client send comment pings. for node: `req.setSocketKeepAlive(true, 30000)` or use fetch wrappers that send `:\n` every 10s. also recommend exponential backoff on reconnect with jitter to avoid thundering herd.

maria (Support): sent that to customer A, they replied it's a bandaid — want platform fix.

jin (Eng-runtime): roadmap proposal (short):
- P0: enable server comment pings (12s) across hosted, ensure proxy passthrough (2d)
- P1: implement `stream_id` + `offset` resume + 10m cursor cache (1 sprint)
- P1: expose `connection_liveness` metric (last ping received per connection) and alert on spike of `no-ping > 45s` (for SRE ops)
- P2: billing change: mark server-initiated aborts as non-retryable for billing credits or automatic refund service (requires billing + legal)

carla (Billing): booking time: need to run impact analysis before we auto-credit. can we at least tag aborted streams so we can query and manually credit high-priority customers?

jin (Eng-runtime): we can add a `stream_abort_reason` tag to logs/metrics. set `abort_due_to_inactivity` boolean.

alex (SRE): also log the L4 LBs connection state transitions and any `RST` from external networks — helps debug midstream resets.

maria (Support): requests from escalations: detailed repro playbook + temporary policy to suspend billing while we investigate for affected accounts. can we do that?

carla (Billing): yes we can do manual suspends for verified escalations. hit me with account IDs and rough token counts. we'll hold charges pending root cause.

jin (Eng-runtime): implementation notes for engineers (copy):
```
# server-side SSE ping pseudo
while connection open:
  sleep(12s)
  write(":\\n")  # SSE comment ping
  flush()
```
Also ensure we don't use `Connection: close` and that we `flush` after writing. add tests: simulate a 40s client pause behind our proxies.
```
# client recon header example
Last-Event-ID: stream123:456
```
```
# sample log line
stream_id=stream123 offset=456 status=aborted reason=abort_due_to_inactivity duration_s=92
```

alex (SRE): tests we should run in staging:
- client pause 0-120s behind LB and nginx to ensure pings survive
- simulate high token bursts to ensure pings don't interfere with payload framing
- reconnect resume with duplicate offsets to validate dedupe

maria (Support): i'll assemble the repro bundles and customer logs and ping this thread. i'll also send customers the temporary client suggestions.

carla (Billing): tagging: please add `billing_impact=yes` for affected streams in logs so we can pull reports.

incidents-bot: /incident create streaming-heartbeat-xx auto-detected spike in disconnects (sev=3) by maria.

jin (Eng-runtime): thanks. i'll start a quick PR for comment pings and a staging test harness. will loop in alex for proxy validation.

maria (Support): thanks all — keeping this thread updated with customer replies. :thumbsup:
